THE VOICE OF THE CARRY · SILENT BY DEFAULT · THE RATIO IS THE SKY'S, THE REGISTER IS THE EAR'S
The sky lifted off, the plate read for its own engraving: the true astrolabe was always a kit, the engraved plate beneath and the openwork rete of the heavens turning above it, and studying the instrument meant removing the sky and turning the plate in the hand. Touch a card and its answer lights at the exact antipode, the axis through the still centre where every dyad sums to zero. THE NOT turns the plate half a round: the reflection the quantum globe forbids, lawful on the poles. THE OCTAVE steps every card to its doubled seat: eighteen presses close the long orbit, the Seed still, the pendulum swinging, the hexad circling in six.

COMPOSED, NEVER CAST · A RHYME WITH THE GLOBE, NEVER AN AUTHORITY · THE ZERO EVERY DYAD SUMS TO

THE FACE, READ

THE PLATEThe rosette of the twenty-seven: the deck as the discrete three-torus, its original even shape carrying the cube's own order. Shells stand at the square roots of one, two, and three by restlessness; every middle card stands at the exact bisector of its parents; the Scar and the Return, invisible down their own diagonal, hold the vertical; every diameter joins a card to its answer; the Seed at the centre is the unknot, unlit within. The plate is the flat pose of a solid: the cube in the hand performs the passage.
THE RINGThe year around the plate: twelve folds, the four stations standing taller among them. Longitude runs anticlockwise from the spring crossing.
THE SUN · THE MOONThe two lights walking the ring at their own speeds: the sun once a year, the moon once a month. Their joint position with the spin is the moment's coordinate.
THE DRAGONTwo open silver circles: the head, and the tail drawn dashed. The empty crossings where eclipses strike, and they walk the ring backward, one full lap in eighteen years and seven months.
THE STANDING CELLThe breathing white-gold ring: where this hour lives on the frame. The month walks time, the day walks depth, the hour walks state. Derived from the clock, never drawn.
THE TRACEThe standing cell's recent walk, cooling toward the past. The sky's periods never divide evenly, so the walk revisits everything and never once repeats.
THE CARRYEvery rollover passes through the null: when a count completes and returns home, the Seed's rim flashes once. The calendar keeps time by returning to its still point.
THE MOON'S CELLThe dashed silver ring on the plate: her longitude divided by twenty-seven, one cell a day on her lap against the stars. A coordinate, not a station.
THE VOICETwo tones slightly off a consonance throb at their difference: the remainder made audible. The comma is the tuning's carry, the epact the calendar's, and the two moons are the sidereal month against the synodic: the sun's own walk, heard as a slow beat an octave down.
THE MOON'S PHASEThe moon marker wears her lit fraction. At the dark she becomes the Seed's own form, the unlit ring, and the frame's null echoes her: the month passing its seam. At the full she stands haloed at the antipode. The two pins of the cycle, forced and not chosen; near either, the syzygy chord joins the two lights.
THE DRAGON'S WINDOWWhen the sun stands within fifteen degrees of a crossing, the open window is drawn as an arc about it: the season in which eclipses are possible, at the pins and only at the pins. Geometry, never counsel.

WHAT IT IS · WHAT IT IS FOR

The sky keeps exactly three clocks: the spin, the moon, the orbit. The deck keeps exactly three layers, ordered by speed. Seated by speed they take their places without being told, and the moment becomes a coordinate on the frame the way a shoreline gives a bearing. That is all the instrument does, and all it will ever claim to do.

It is a calendar that faces backward. Every calendar in the astrological tradition is a forecast instrument; this one is built the other way, toward record and toward the present moment. Scrub the sliders to any hour and watch where it stands, or turn the crank and let every wheel run at once: the watch, the moon's phase, the sun's year and the dragon's slow regression, all at their true ratios from one handle. Turn it gently and the cells walk one by one. Turn it further and the moon lives her whole phase while the sun creeps. Further still and the year turns, the dark moons marching round the ring until one steps inside the window, which is the eclipse seasons showing themselves. The fast wheels blur as a cranked orrery's do: that is not a fault, it is what speed looks like on a real machine. Sound the beats and hear what a remainder is. The dragon keeps its appointments, the stations come round, and none of it ever says what to do: there is no auspicious hour and no forbidden one.

Tested against the sky: run over eight centuries of computed eclipses, every one falls where the crossing-layer is still, and among central solar eclipses the near band of the distance layer called totality with full precision, four hundred and twenty-four totals against not one annular, while the partial eclipses, which do not depend on distance, showed no preference at all. A claimed coincidence at the band edge was tested, found to be an arithmetic error, and retracted. The whole record, the claim, its overturning, and its remeasurement, stands in the chart, sections XI to XIV, kept whole because how a finding was reached is part of the finding.

THE CALENDAR · THE SKY'S NEXT OBSERVANCES

The sky's carries, public and universal, marked as they approach. Every date below is computed from the pinned ephemeris at its honest tolerance of about a day, and every one is an event of the cycle, never advice about the day: there is no auspicious hour and no forbidden one.

    THE LOG · THE HAND’S OWN TRACK

    Casts as fixes on the year-torus: each committed reading pinned where the sky stood when it was witnessed, the sun’s longitude across, the moon’s elongation down. The marks are read from the bench’s own journal exactly as stamped at commit, and the two pins rule the surface: the dark moon along the seam, the full along the middle. A faint thread joins the track in the order it was walked, and recurrence shows as geometry. Local and unmined, one hand’s mirror, never a profile.

    THE VESSEL’S OWN · THIS BROWSER ONLY · NEVER SENT · READ, NEVER RESTAMPED

    PATHWAYS · NOT YET BUILT

    • THE WAYFINDER'S WEATHER. The trace and the carry flash as an ambient layer around the reading surface, kept strictly apart from the cast: the one cast, once, is never touched by the clock.
    • PROPER LUNAR THEORY. The ephemeris has graduated to its own module and is pinned by test against real eclipses (luminaraSky.test.ts), at the linear terms' honest tolerance of a few degrees. The remaining pathway is precision: perturbation terms, if the instrument ever needs the almanac's own day.
    • THE BOUNDARY STONE. The moon's daily cell is shown as a coordinate, freely. Stations, a card for each day read as a meaning, are an assignment, and stand behind the chart's boundary stone until the architect moves it.

    OPEN QUESTIONS

    • What is an edge, for time? The dyad diameters are involution; shell neighbours are adjacency; the becoming is a gradient. Which of these should the standing cell's arrival excite?
    • The trace is a path on the rosette. Should the Wayfinder keep it, fade it, or fold it into the constellation it already draws?
    • Every rollover passes through the null. Is the carry flash a teaching surface, or noise?
    • The pulse here decays by hand. If activations ever mean anything, they must be derived, and pinned, or not exist.
